CLASS 29 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Storytime & Pre-Reading Comprehension

Age 4–5 YearsClass 29 of 30Adventures 29 story gamesSight words 52 lessonsSubjects Sequencing · feelings · retelling

Build early reading comprehension through picture stories, sequencing, predictions, characters, emotions, memory, and problem-solving. Twenty-nine draw-on-the-picture adventures — every one played on its own storybook illustration, with plain written instructions and a printable worksheet twin in the Reading worksheet library.

No reading needed: every adventure is one big picture to draw on, with plain instructions a grown-up can read aloud. Grown-ups get the story behind each activity on its page.

Meet the adventures ↓ Learn the sight words ↓One or two stories per sitting is a full session.
PLAY · THE 29 STORYTIME ADVENTURES

Twenty-nine story adventures.

Start anywhere your child’s curiosity points. The shelves run in a gentle skill order — sequences before inferences — but every game stands alone. Each adventure twins with a printable worksheet at /worksheets/reading/.

LEARN · 52 SIGHT WORD LESSONS

Learn the sight words, one card at a time.

The small words on every page of a first book: a, the, I, can, see, blue and more. Tap any card to open its lesson: the flashcard with a drawing canvas on the left, and on the right how to teach the word, how to say it and where to use it. Start at the top and work down, three new words a day at most.

ATheIYouMeMyWeItIsAmAreBeCanAndInToUpDownGoComeCameRunJumpPlaySeeLookFindHelpMakeBigLittleFunnyOneTwoThreeBlueYellowBlackBrownHereWhereAwayAtByForNotButAllSaidAteDidCould

The whole shelf also lives on the Sight Words hub — one page with all fifty-two lessons. Every lesson pairs with a printable card in the Sight Words flashcard set, with its own download button and notes for grown-ups.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Story play at bedtime and in the car.

Retell the day in three

  • Bedtime recap in three steps: first we…, then we…, last we…. Sequencing practice with your own day.
  • Let your child pick the three — their order, their story.

What happens next?

  • Pause a picture book before the last page and guess the ending — exactly what Dragon’s Ending Studio plays.
  • Silly endings welcome; then find the one that fits.

Comprehension grows from talking about stories, not from quizzing them. Follow the “why do you think so?” wherever it leads.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Pre-reading comprehension is talking, not testing: who is this about, where are we, what happened first, what happens next? Every game here asks one of those questions with pictures instead of print, and speaks its instructions aloud so no reading is required to play.

The worksheets are the paper twins — the same picture stories with room to retell, draw and write. Browse the reading worksheets and print the adventure your child loved. Playing games never marks a class complete; only real game finishes do, and only for the child chosen in My Classroom.
